meaning: Plausible in-vivo adult Drosophila spike-rate ranges (Hz, population mean per cell over the window). spontaneous_hz applies to baseline windows, driven_hz to stimulus windows. A bound is a sanity range, not a target. verified:true means both ends of both intervals rest on values read from the cited sources, or are wider than every read value (the basis names the widest read value). A value counts as read when it was taken from text, from a numeric data file, from the coordinates in a vector figure, or computed from deposited raw recordings with a committed script; a raster image or an axis limit never counts. kind:model_health marks a declared limit on the model itself that makes no physiological claim, because no primary source measures the quantity; it is marked verified:true in the same sense as the spec gates O5-O7 (causal controls of the model), and its basis says so.

ORN.basis: spontaneous: Hallem 2006 empty-neuron SFR 1-47 Hz for 24 Ors (DoOR.data), Hallem 2006 text 'receptors with spontaneous firing rates of <5 spikes/s (Or9a, Or22a, Or43b, Or47a, and Or59b)'; Kazama & Wilson 2008 'ORNs fire spontaneously at about 7 spikes/s' (VM2). driven: Hallem 2006 '69 ... 3%, resulted in very strong responses of >=200 spikes/s' (500 ms window, spontaneous subtracted, 1e-2 dilution); Kazama & Wilson 2008 'odors can easily trigger sustained ORN firing rates well above 200 spikes/s'; 300 Hz ceiling = 'the maximum ORN firing rate (~300 spikes/s)' in Wilson 2013 (review, secondary for Hallem 2006).

PN.basis: spontaneous: Turner, Bazhenov & Laurent 2008 Fig. 3F legend 'spontaneous spike rates in PNs (4.6 +/- 4.2 s^-1, n = 37 PNs)'; 20 Hz upper end is mean + ~3.7 SD and above the pre-odour baselines of Bhandawat 2007 Supp. Fig. 2 (4-23 Hz, one panel at the edge). driven, for windows of 0.5 s or longer (the T-maze stimulus window is 2 s of constant odour): Olsen, Bhandawat & Wilson 2010 Methods 'R max = 165 spikes/sec' (fitted saturating response over the 500-msec stimulus); Bhandawat 2007 Supp. Fig. 2 (vector PDF, 140 PSTHs) highest 0-0.5 s mean ~184 Hz; Kazama & Wilson 2009 text '>150 spikes/sec'. 250 Hz is above every read average over 0.5 s or more. Shorter windows go higher: Bhandawat 2007 Fig. 6 (100 ms peak epoch) up to ~250-265 Hz, 50 ms PSTH peaks up to ~314 Hz, so this ceiling must not be applied to windows shorter than 0.5 s.

KC.basis: spontaneous: Turner 2008 p.736 'very low spontaneous firing (0.1 +/- 0.4 spike/s)'. driven: Turner 2008 'a given odor evoked a spiking response in only 6 +/- 5% of the cells' (n = 71), responders fire 'alpha'/beta' 4.9 +/- 3.0 spikes ... alpha/beta 2.2 +/- 1.2' in the 0-2 s window; Murthy, Fiete & Laurent 2008: up to 49% of GFP- KCs respond under a >=1-spike criterion, 'with few spikes'. Even if every KC fired like an alpha'/beta' responder (4.9 spikes / 2 s = 2.45 Hz) the population mean would be ~2.5 Hz; the 5 Hz ceiling is twice that. Changed from v1 (20 Hz), which no source supported.

MBON.basis: spontaneous: Vrontou 2021 Fig. 2 (vector PDF; 1 s before odour, whole-cell in vivo) MBON-alpha2sc mean 1.8 (0-9.2) Hz n = 20, MBON-gamma1pedc>alpha/beta 5.8 (0.1-17.9) Hz n = 33, MBON-beta1>alpha 7.9 (0-37.4) Hz n = 29; Yamada 2023 Fig. 3-fs2 source data, MBON-alpha1 pre-odour 4.7-9.6 Hz; Nanami 2024 deposited MBON-alpha1 recording (our re-analysis) 8.4 +/- 3.6 Hz. 40 Hz is above the highest single cell (37.4). driven: Vrontou 2021 on-response (750 ms window) up to 149.1 Hz (gamma1pedc), 122 Hz (beta1>alpha); Hige 2015 Neuron '118 +/- 8.3 spikes' in 0-1.4 s above baseline; Nanami 2024 data OCT 1 s 106-120 Hz, 100 ms bins up to 160 Hz; Vrontou 2021 Fig. 1 optogenetic Kenyon-cell drive up to ~180 Hz (MBON-alpha2sc). 180 Hz covers every read value in any window and any drive. The ex-vivo MBON-alpha3 12.1 Hz (Hafez 2023) is consistent but not used.

DNa02.basis: spontaneous: Yang 2024 Fig. S7A (vector PDF, n = 4 flies), per-fly mean rate while not walking 7.8, 11.8, 18.3, 38.5 Hz (group mean 19.1); Rayshubskiy 2025 deposited recordings (7 cells, our re-analysis with the authors' spike detector): quietest 10% of seconds 0.1-7.2 Hz, whole-recording means 1.6-9.7 Hz; Rayshubskiy 2025 text 'DNa02 has a relatively high basal firing rate' and 'hyperpolarizes during immobility'. 0 Hz is below every read value; 40 Hz is above the highest (38.5). driven: Yang 2024 text 'this stride-locked firing rate modulation was only about 15 spikes/sec (approximately 10% of the cell's dynamic range)', i.e. a ~150 spikes/s range; walking per-fly means 35.2-76.4 Hz (Fig. S7A); busiest 1 s bins 93-128 Hz (135 Hz at a looser spike threshold) in the Rayshubskiy recordings. No DNa02 recording under visual motion was found, so this is the cell's recorded range in any state (walking in the dark, odour, heat). Derivation: sources/dna02_rates_read.json.

GF.basis: spontaneous: 0 spikes in 502 s of pre-loom baseline across 251 whole-cell traces from 27 flies (Dombrovski 2025 deposited data, our re-analysis; 95% upper limit ~0.006 Hz); recordings are kept only with resting potential below -55 mV (Ache 2019) or -50 mV (Jang 2023). 1 Hz is above every read value. driven: Dombrovski 2023 Results 'DNp02, DNp11, the GF and DNp04 all depolarized in response to looming, and all except the GF produced action potentials' (150 ms window, n = 7 flies); 0 spikes per loom in the 251 Dombrovski 2025 traces; Mu 2014 'None of the visual and mechanical stimuli used in our experiments initiated action potentials'; when it does fire, the GF 'fires a single action potential' (Ache 2019 Nat Neurosci), i.e. at most ~7 Hz over a 150 ms window. 50 Hz is above every read value. Papers showing looming-evoked GF spikes (von Reyn 2014, 2017; Ache 2019 Curr Biol) remain unread.

LC_looming.basis: UNVERIFIED and probably not a spiking quantity: the only readable electrophysiology of lobula output neurons, including LPLC2-like cells projecting to the GF glomerulus, says they 'conduct only by electrotonic transmission; they show both fast and slow membrane potential fluctuations but never spike, even when injected with depolarizing current' (Mu 2012; read via WebFetch, abstract directly). Every other study read (von Reyn 2017, Ache 2019, Klapoetke 2017, Morimoto 2020, Keles 2020, Tanaka & Clark 2020/2022) used calcium imaging; Kim 2023 Curr Biol reports spike rates for DNp06, not LPLC2 (not readable). No LC4 or LPLC2 rate in Hz exists in anything read. As with HS, a LIF proxy can only pass the signal by spiking, so this bound tests the model class; numbers are declared.

LPTC.cell_types: HS (HSN, HSE, HSS); the optomotor spec checks HS only
LPTC.basis: UNVERIFIED: HS cells respond with graded potentials; Fujiwara et al. 2017 call them non-spiking during walking; Joesch 2008 (VS) reports graded responses 'superimposed by small action potentials of irregular amplitude'. Schnell et al. 2010 recorded HSN, HSE and HSS (not H2, as v1 implied) and only its abstract was readable. No HS spike rate in Hz was found. The LIF proxy can only spike, so this bound tests that it does not spike at high rates; the numbers are declared.

brain_mean.basis: MODEL-HEALTH LIMIT, not a physiological claim: no primary source measures a brain-wide mean spike rate in the fly. It catches runaway activity (the v1 runaway had a ~6 Hz mean). Context only: an energy-budget estimate gives a maximum average of ~4 Hz, called 'highly approximate, illustrative' by its authors (Zanichelli et al. 2025, State of Brain Emulation Report, arXiv 2510.15745, from Neville 2018 oxygen use and Laughlin 1998 spike cost); measured population rates that exist are low (KC 0.1 +/- 0.4 Hz, PN 4.6 +/- 4.2 Hz, Turner 2008). Shiu 2024 used 0 Hz baselines and warns absolute rates are unreliable.

brain_max_single_neuron.basis: MODEL-HEALTH LIMIT, not a physiological claim: no neuron sustains above 300 Hz over a window, below the 1/t_ref ~ 450 Hz ceiling where LIF output saturates. It cannot be a verified physiological ceiling: nothing can show that no fly neuron exceeds it. Context: the highest read window-averaged rate is ~293 Hz (Or67c to ethyl lactate, 500 ms, Hallem 2006 data as redistributed in Tesileanu et al. eLife 39279, flyResponsesWithNames.mat); ORN peaks in 50 ms bins exceed 400 Hz (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.27.662059) and PN 50 ms PSTH peaks reach ~314 Hz (Bhandawat 2007), so a real neuron can exceed 300 Hz over windows shorter than 0.5 s.

literature_check.method: primary sources read via web (full text where open); every value below was read, none recalled. Blind: no simulation output was consulted.
literature_check.access_failures: Wilson 2004 (Science) and Bhandawat 2007 (Nat Neurosci) full text not reachable (paywall; PMC captcha; Europe PMC rate limit). von Reyn 2014 main text paywalled. Schnell 2010 full text 403.

changes_from_v2: DNa02: verified from recordings (Yang 2024, Rayshubskiy 2025 data); spontaneous 0-20 -> 0-40 Hz, driven 0-100 -> 0-150 Hz.
PN: driven ceiling 250 Hz now verified for windows of 0.5 s or longer (Bhandawat 2007, Olsen 2010, Kazama & Wilson 2009); numbers unchanged.
MBON: verified from in-vivo recordings (Vrontou 2021, Yamada 2023, Nanami 2024 data); spontaneous 0-30 -> 0-40 Hz, driven 0-150 -> 0-180 Hz.
GF: verified (Dombrovski 2023, Dombrovski 2025 data, Mu 2014, Ache 2019); numbers unchanged.
LC_looming: still unverified; the only readable electrophysiology says lobula output neurons do not spike (Mu 2012).
brain_mean, brain_max_single_neuron: numbers unchanged; declared kind:model_health, since no source measures them.
Every choice was made blind: no receipt, record or simulation output of any paradigm was opened.
